description: Create comprehensive old-vs-new latency comparison benchmark tests that simulate both the sequential (old) and parallel/optimized (new) code paths, producing concrete timing numbers for chat endpoint and page load scenarios.
steps:
Create apps/backend/tests/test_latency_comparison.py with these benchmark scenarios:
  (a) Chat endpoint - OLD sequential path: simulate retrieve_context (150ms) then load_conversation_history (100ms) then rate_limit with 4 individual Redis calls (25ms each = 100ms) = total ~350ms sequential
  (b) Chat endpoint - NEW parallel path: simulate retrieve_context (150ms) + load_conversation_history (100ms) via asyncio.gather (max = 150ms) + rate_limit via pipeline (1 call = 25ms) + edge trust skipping burst = total ~175ms
  (c) Page load - OLD path: simulate 3 middleware call_next chains (15ms each = 45ms overhead) + no warm-up so first Azure Search adds cold start (200ms DNS/TLS)
  (d) Page load - NEW path: simulate 1 unified middleware (15ms) + warm-up already done (0ms cold start)
  (e) Print a comparison table at end showing old vs new with % improvement
  Each test should use AsyncMock with asyncio.sleep for controlled delays, measure wall-clock time, and assert the new path is significantly faster than old path (at least 40% improvement for chat, at least 50% for page load).

Create apps/edge/tests/latency-comparison.test.ts with these benchmark scenarios:
  (a) OLD edge flow: rate limit check (KV get) + separate burst check (another KV get) + proxy without X-Rate-Limited-By header = backend does full rate limit again
  (b) NEW edge flow: rate limit check (single KV get+put) + sets X-Rate-Limited-By header = backend skips burst check
  (c) Measure: mock KV with 5ms delay per operation, measure total edge processing time for 100 requests in old vs new flow
  (d) Assert new flow uses fewer KV operations and total time is at least 30% lower
  (e) Include a describe block 'Latency Comparison Summary' that logs a formatted table with old vs new timings.

Create apps/frontend/src/__tests__/latency-comparison.test.jsx with page load comparison:
  (a) OLD: simulate 3 sequential fetch calls for initial page data (auth check, user preferences, initial content) = 3 * 80ms = 240ms
  (b) NEW: simulate Promise.all for the same 3 fetches = max(80ms) = 80ms (parallel)
  (c) Assert the new approach is at least 60% faster
  (d) Document: middleware reduction (3 -> 1) saves ~30ms per request at edge
  (e) Print comparison summary
acceptance_criteria: Running `cd apps/backend && APP_ENV=test JWT_SECRET=test-secret-at-least-32-characters-long-for-ci python -m pytest tests/test_latency_comparison.py -v` passes all tests
Running `cd apps/edge && pnpm test -- tests/latency-comparison.test.ts` passes all tests
Running `cd apps/frontend && pnpm test -- src/__tests__/latency-comparison.test.jsx` passes all tests
Each test file produces clearly labeled timing output (old: Xms, new: Yms, improvement: Z%)
Backend chat benchmark shows at least 40% improvement (old ~350ms vs new ~175ms)
Page load benchmark shows at least 50% improvement
Tests are deterministic - use controlled sleep/delay values, not real network calls
